data.name: Mansingh
data.gender_notes: Mansingh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mansingh is derived from two Sanskrit words: ‘Man’ meaning Moon and ‘Singh’ meaning Lion. This name is believed to represent the God of Man, a powerful protector and leader. It is often given to boys born under the influence of the moon. The name Mansingh carries the meaning “Moon, God of Man” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mansingh usually hope their child will grow to embody moon, god of man and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name with divine origin, reflecting the power and protection of the moon and the strength and courage of the lion.
data.etymology: Mansingh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon, God of Man.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mansingh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mansingh carries a distinguished heritage with strong cultural roots in India. It is a revered and historic name associated with renowned warriors and powerful rulers in Hindu mythology and history. Legendary figures like Maharaja Mansingh Chauhan, the Rajput king of the Chauhan clan, and Maharaja Mansingh of Jaipur are celebrated for their bravery, leadership, and strength, reflecting the power and resilience embodied by the name.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Mansingh represents the divine union of the masculine and feminine energies symbolized by the lion (Masculine) and the moon (Feminine). It invokes the protection, strength, and fearlessness of the lion, while the calm, nurturing, and intuitive qualities of the moon. The name is said to be bestowed by the gods, empowering the bearer with their blessings, and instilling valor, wisdom, and an indomitable spirit.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mansingh: Servant of God's Mind or Intelligence. The name Mansingh signifies a devoted soul, surrendered to the divine wisdom and consciousness of the universe. It symbolizes the inner quest for knowledge and understanding, and the constant endeavor to align one's thoughts and actions with the divine will.

historical_references.reference: Mansingh I (r. 1586-1607 CE): A Maratha king of the Bhosle dynasty, Mansingh is noted for expanding the Maratha territories in Maharashtra and beyond, and for challenging the Mughal empire in central India.
historical_references.context: Mansingh I is often regarded as the founder of the Maratha Empire, which would go on to become a major power in Indian history.

historical_references.reference: Mansingh II (r. 1660-1680 CE): A Maratha king of the Bhosle dynasty, Mansingh II played a key role in the Battle of Panipat (1665 CE), in which the Marathas were initially victorious but later suffered heavy losses. Despite this setback, Mansingh II continued to assert Maratha power and influence in northern India.
historical_references.context: Mansingh II is remembered for his military prowess and his efforts to expand the Maratha Empire beyond its traditional heartlands in Maharashtra.
